annotations.title: Buffer, merge, clip or simplify features

description: Use this when the user wants to apply one GIS operation to a set of features (an uploaded file, a link, inline GeoJSON, or a download link from another TerraLab answer) and get the result as a file: buffer every feature by radius_m, union (dissolve all features into one, or one per value of dissolve_field), intersection or difference with a second layer, clip to a second layer or to an area (place, place with radius_m, or bbox), simplify by tolerance_m, centroid of each feature, or area_length (adds area_m2, perimeter_m and length_m to each feature, geodesic). Overlays run in WGS 84 degrees; buffer, simplify and centroid in a local equidistant projection. Up to 20,000 features and 100,000 vertices (10,000 for buffer). Returns the feature count, geometry types, total area or length, a map and GeoJSON, KML, Shapefile zip, GeoPackage and CSV downloads. Not for one distance or the area of a shape drawn in the chat: that is measure. Not for reading or converting a file without changing its geometry: that is open_gis_file. Never use the user's current location unless they type it. Download links build their file when opened; no file is saved. Never pass these links to open_gis_file: list every format the user needs in formats, in this one call. TerraLab reads the file or link to answer and keeps no copy.

area.description: For clip: the area to keep, as a bbox or a place with a radius (its bounding box is used). The place the user asks about, not the user's own location.

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees (WGS 84).

place.description: A place name or address, or a point.

radius_m.description: Radius around the place in metres.

dissolve_field.description: For union: dissolve into one feature per value of this field instead of one feature.

file.description: A file uploaded in the conversation (GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, zipped Shapefile, CSV or WKT).

formats.description: Download formats. All five by default.

geojson.description: The features as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, Feature or geometry in WGS 84 (longitude, latitude).

radius_m.description: For buffer: the distance in metres (convert km or miles first).

title.description: Name for the map and the output files.

tolerance_m.description: For simplify: the largest allowed shift of the outline in metres.

url.description: A public http(s) link to the features, or a TerraLab download link from an earlier answer.

with_file.description: For intersection, difference and clip: the second layer, uploaded in the conversation.

with_geojson.description: For intersection, difference and clip: the second layer as GeoJSON in WGS 84. Only its polygons count.

with_url.description: For intersection, difference and clip: a link to the second layer, or a TerraLab download link.

name: process_geometry

downloads.description: Download links; each builds its file when opened.

hint.description: What to do next, on errors only.

sources.description: Data sources and licences of the result.
